title: When China Gets Its Own Mythos
gist: A former U.S. Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy argues that frontier AI models (Anthropic's Claude Mythos, OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber) have collapsed the specialist bottleneck in offensive cyber, leaving the U.S. only nine to 12 months before China fields an equivalent capability and can hold water, power and transit systems at risk at scale. He calls for preemptive disruption of Chinese distillation and chip-smuggling networks, a once-in-a-generation cyberdefense appropriation, and a shift from patching to physical-consequence resilience anchored at Idaho National Laboratory.

insights.claim: Anthropic disclosed in April 2026 that its frontier model Claude Mythos can find and exploit software vulnerabilities better than all but the most skilled humans, including a flaw that had gone undetected for 27 years in a secure operating system used to run firewalls guarding sensitive networks.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: A capability step-change in AI-assisted exploitation resets the demand curve for cyberdefense spend and for vulnerability-management vendors; the 27-year-old firewall OS flaw is evidence the installed base is far leakier than audits imply.
insights.quote: could find and exploit security vulnerabilities in software better than “all but the most skilled humans.”
insights.locator: In April, Anthropic disclosed that its newest frontier AI model

insights.claim: Allegations that Anthropic's Mythos warnings were mere marketing are undercut by leading commercial software companies given early access corroborating the capability claim.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Third-party corroboration means capability claims should be underwritten rather than discounted as vendor hype when sizing cyber budgets.
insights.locator: Despite some allegations that Anthropic’s warnings about Mythos

insights.claim: Work in vulnerability discovery that long belonged to a small class of elite specialists can now be done by AI faster and at greater scale than human teams or earlier automated tools, removing the scarcity constraint that historically capped the top end of the attacker-defender contest.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Labor-scarcity moats in offensive and defensive security services erode; value shifts to whoever controls model access and to remediation/resilience capacity.
insights.locator: FIRST-MOVER ADVANTAGE

insights.claim: Microsoft, using an internal scanning system built on multiple models, disclosed sixteen previously undetected flaws in the Windows networking stack, and Palo Alto Networks reported finding far more vulnerabilities in a single scan of its own products than it typically discloses in a month.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Concrete throughput evidence: expect a step-change in disclosed CVE volume, which stresses patch-management and vulnerability-triage vendors and raises disclosure-driven headline risk for software incumbents.
insights.quote: reported finding far more vulnerabilities in a single scan than it typically discloses in a month
insights.locator: Within weeks of Anthropic launching Project Glasswing

insights.claim: The hardest step in infrastructure attacks has historically been converting IT network access into reliable control of physical equipment, because it required specialists fluent in a particular vendor's proprietary control systems; a model that can read obscure industrial firmware turns that months-long specialist task into a routine one.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: OT/ICS security, not IT security, becomes the binding constraint; watch demand for OT-specific monitoring, segmentation and safety-system vendors.
insights.quote: threatens to turn the hardest part of designing an infrastructure attack into a routine task
insights.locator: That final step has historically remained dependent

insights.claim: In 2017 hackers linked by the U.S. Justice Department to a Russian military research institute penetrated a Saudi petrochemical plant and tried to disable its safety instrumented systems, but their code failed to account for the exact behavior of the plant's specific safety controllers and tripped a protective shutdown, exposing the operation before physical harm occurred.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: The historical failure mode was vendor-specific engineering ignorance — precisely the gap AI now closes, so past near-misses are a poor guide to future hit rates.
insights.locator: In 2017, for instance, hackers that the U.S. Department of Justice linked

insights.claim: The United States may have only nine to 12 months to protect its critical infrastructure before adversaries wield AI models capable of automated vulnerability discovery and exploitation.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: An explicit timeline from a former Pentagon cyber policy chief sets the horizon for emergency appropriations, utility capex and OT-security procurement cycles.
insights.quote: The United States may only have nine to 12 months to protect its critical infrastructure from AI-powered attacks.
insights.locator: As firms use Mythos to hunt and fix flaws

insights.claim: The most capable cyber-vulnerability discovery tools currently belong to defenders — described as the best news in cybersecurity in decades — because only two American companies, Anthropic and OpenAI, have demonstrated such models and both restrict them to defensive work.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: The defender advantage is a policy artifact of two firms' access decisions, not a structural moat — it can vanish with one open-weight release or leak.
insights.quote: At the moment, the most capable cybervulnerability discovery tools belong to defenders. This is the best news in cybersecurity in decades.
insights.locator: WITHIN STRIKING DISTANCE

insights.claim: The dominant risk is not a single catastrophic cyber–Pearl Harbor but cheap, rapid acquisition of footholds across many water, power and transit systems that adversaries can hold at risk to deter, extort, or simply wait.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Reframes the tail risk from one insurable mega-event to persistent distributed hostage-taking — which is far harder to price for cyber insurers and utility credit.
insights.quote: The risk is not a single massive strike on a piece of key infrastructure, a cyber–Pearl Harbor, but a world in which China and others can cheaply and quickly gain footholds across far more of the systems that run daily life
insights.locator: That would allow for a kind of cyberattack different from any prior one

insights.claim: Every month that an adversary can siphon capability from U.S. models or gain access to more advanced chips is a month subtracted from the defenders' head start, making export-control enforcement and anti-distillation measures directly equivalent to defensive time.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Gives a clean mental model for pricing enforcement news: chip-smuggling prosecutions and distillation crackdowns are literally buying defensive runway.
insights.quote: each month that an adversary can siphon abilities from U.S. models and gain access to more advanced chips is a month subtracted from the defenders’ head start
insights.locator: exposed on all flanks

insights.claim: Advanced AI sharpens an instrument Beijing already prizes: threatening Taiwan's critical infrastructure and that of would-be defenders in order to deter a fight before it begins.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: AI cyber capability is a Taiwan-deterrence variable, not just an IT-risk variable — it raises the probability of coercion short of kinetic conflict, which markets price differently.
insights.locator: Advanced AI will sharpen an instrument that Beijing already prizes

insights.claim: Anthropic withheld Mythos from open release and instead gave defenders first access through Project Glasswing, a restricted coalition of technology, finance and open-source organizations, later releasing a guardrailed version called Fable to the public.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: A commercial firm voluntarily forgoing revenue on its most powerful product sets a precedent that could be codified into release regulation — a direct constraint on frontier-lab monetization timelines.
insights.quote: a company chose to withhold its most powerful product from broad release because the product could be turned, with little modification, into a weapon
insights.locator: Understanding the danger, Anthropic has not released Mythos openly

insights.claim: OpenAI made GPT-5.5-Cyber available to vetted security teams within weeks of Project Glasswing through a program called Trusted Access for Cyber, indicating vetted-access tiers are becoming the industry norm for cyber-capable frontier models.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Gated distribution creates a new commercial channel — inclusion in these coalitions becomes a competitive advantage for security vendors and infrastructure suppliers.
insights.locator: Within weeks of Anthropic launching Project Glasswing

insights.claim: A structural asymmetry in intelligence exists because private firms must publicize models to monetize them while governments have every incentive to conceal national-security AI systems, so U.S. policymakers may not know when China reaches Mythos-class capability.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Assume any observed Chinese capability lags the real one; positioning should not wait for public confirmation of parity.
insights.quote: U.S. policymakers may not know when China gets a Mythos-class model.
insights.locator: But U.S. policymakers may not know when China achieves that capability

insights.claim: On June 2, 2026 President Trump signed an executive order creating a voluntary framework giving the U.S. government up to 30 days of early access to new frontier models before broader release, plus security enhancements for federal IT networks.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: A 30-day pre-release government window is the first concrete regulatory drag on frontier model launch cadence; watch whether it becomes mandatory.
insights.locator: BATTEN THE HATCHES

themes.theme: China's four routes to a Mythos-class model

insights.claim: About a day after the U.S. government temporarily banned foreign access to Anthropic's newly released Mythos and Fable models in mid-June 2026, the Chinese company Zhipu AI released GLM-5.2, an open-weight model it claims competes with Anthropic's second-best model Opus on certain benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Chinese labs are timing open-weight releases to U.S. access restrictions, converting American export policy into their own distribution advantage.
insights.locator: Recent developments suggest that China is getting close

insights.claim: Open-weight models such as GLM-5.2 can be downloaded and deployed without permission from the maker or reliance on infrastructure the U.S. government can control, and any safeguards can be easily removed — making them usable for almost any purpose at a fraction of the cost of advanced American models.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Open weights structurally defeat access-control policy and undercut U.S. model pricing simultaneously — the key vulnerability in any gated-release strategy.
insights.quote: Any safeguards can be easily removed.
insights.locator: Unlike Mythos or OpenAI’s most capable models

insights.claim: OpenAI told Congress in a February memo that it observed accounts tied to DeepSeek employees circumventing its access controls to harvest model outputs for distillation, and Anthropic disclosed a comparable campaign that same month.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Documented distillation gives legal and policy grounds for API-level restrictions and entity listings — a tail risk for Chinese AI firms' access to U.S. inference.
insights.locator: The first is illicit or adversarial distillation

insights.claim: Adversarial distillation is presented as the latest chapter in a two-decade Chinese IP-theft campaign that included stealing American Superconductor's wind turbine technology and produced the suspicious resemblance between China's J-31 fighter and the U.S. F-35.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Pattern-matching to past IP theft implies the policy response will follow the same slow arc — and that AI-stack firms face the same equity-destroying exposure American Superconductor did.
insights.locator: Adversarial distillation is just another chapter

insights.claim: Because advanced models are themselves tools for building more capable models, China's use of top U.S. models to engineer its own next generation compounds — an easily missed recursive effect on the capability gap.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Implies the gap narrows non-linearly, so linear extrapolations of Chinese lag are likely too optimistic.
insights.locator: As AI models advance, they become powerful tools

insights.claim: Chip smuggling alone cannot deliver the compute needed to train advanced models — the U.S. Justice Department has prosecuted multiple large smuggling networks in the past year — but China is simultaneously building its own chips.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Smuggling enforcement is necessary but not sufficient; the durable variable is indigenous Chinese fab capacity, which is where to watch for regime change in the compute constraint.
insights.locator: Chinese actors are making efforts to gain illicit access

insights.claim: China's National Intelligence Law requires companies to cooperate with state intelligence collection and the Cyberspace Administration gives the government visibility into model behavior and outputs, so any Chinese lab reaching Mythos-class offensive cyber capability will very likely hand early access to the PLA and intelligence services.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: No civil-military firewall exists in Chinese AI, so commercial-benchmark parity should be read directly as military capability — collapsing the usual lag assumption.
insights.locator: Finally, whenever China acquires new, high-end AI capabilities

insights.claim: In the Volt Typhoon campaign, Chinese state-linked hackers already burrowed deeply into U.S. water, power and transportation organizations, demonstrating prepositioning that AI tooling could activate at scale.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Prepositioning already exists; the new variable is exploitation throughput, which shortens the interval between political crisis and physical disruption.
insights.locator: In a campaign called Volt Typhoon

insights.claim: U.S. critical infrastructure is owned and operated by thousands of small and medium-sized municipal districts and utilities that lack the budget, staff, or leverage to demand secure products from vendors, and carry decades of technical debt in operational technology never designed for internet connectivity.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Fragmented ownership means no market mechanism forces security spend — the fix must be federally funded, which is where the appropriations trade sits.
insights.locator: The United States’ critical infrastructure targets are structurally weak

insights.claim: Because OT firmware fixes require safety revalidation, on-site installation and facility downtime in equipment with a 15-to-25-year lifecycle, a patch engineered today might not be installed until 2030 — an eternity against AI-driven attacks.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: The remediation clock is measured in years while the attack clock is measured in months, so hardening spend will flow to compensating controls and manual-fallback capability rather than patching.
insights.quote: It is therefore possible that a fix designed today and extensively tested for safety wouldn’t be installed until 2030.
insights.locator: Securing this firmware is far more complicated than updating an iPhone

insights.claim: The operators most exposed to the coming AI-attack wave are precisely those least equipped to defend themselves, and no amount of voluntary information-sharing will close that gap.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Dismisses the dominant U.S. policy tool (voluntary info-sharing) as inadequate, implying mandates or direct federal provisioning are the likelier policy path.
insights.quote: The operators most exposed to the coming wave are precisely those least equipped to defend themselves, and no amount of voluntary information-sharing will close that gap.
insights.locator: This is an eternity in an age of AI-driven cyberattacks

insights.claim: In December 2015 Russian hackers who had breached Ukrainian utilities with BlackEnergy malware cut power to over 200,000 customers for several hours, establishing that cyber-to-physical infrastructure disruption is demonstrated rather than hypothetical.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: A concrete precedent and scale benchmark for modeling grid-outage insurance and utility operational risk.
insights.locator: In December 2015, Russian hackers who had breached Ukrainian utilities

insights.claim: Many of the major companies making the control systems that run U.S. water and energy plants, factories and pipelines are headquartered outside the United States, turning domestic infrastructure defense into an alliance-coordination problem.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Foreign-domiciled ICS vendors become policy chokepoints — regulatory pressure and procurement preference may shift toward suppliers subject to U.S. jurisdiction.
insights.locator: Complicating things is the fact that many of the major companies

insights.claim: The U.S. and close partners should use offensive capabilities to disrupt the infrastructure adversaries use to distill and steal American models and obtain export-controlled AI chips, and to degrade hostile prepositioning in U.S. networks before it can be activated.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Advocating preemptive offensive cyber against distillation and smuggling networks raises the escalation baseline and the odds of retaliatory action against U.S. firms.
insights.quote: Now is the time to put policy options on the table that were previously considered out of bounds
insights.locator: The United States and its closest international partners should use the capabilities

insights.claim: Idaho National Laboratory — which in 2007 demonstrated that a cyberattack could physically destroy a diesel generator — is the best candidate to become the dedicated institution coordinating cyberdefense and provisioning concrete defenses to small and medium water, electricity and transportation operators.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Names a specific institutional recipient for a possible large appropriation — a leading indicator of where federal cyber-resilience contracting would flow.
insights.locator: The United States also needs a dedicated institution

insights.claim: Patching is necessary but insufficient because the coming flood of AI-discovered flaws will overwhelm any patching regime and many aging systems will never receive a patch; defenses must be redesigned so a successful intrusion cannot produce a catastrophic physical result, with operators able to run critical services in degraded manual mode.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Shifts the spending thesis from vulnerability scanning and patch tooling toward consequence-limiting engineering and manual-fallback capability.
insights.quote: The coming flood of AI-discovered flaws will overwhelm any patching regime, and for many aging systems, no patch will ever come.
insights.locator: Simply scanning for vulnerabilities will not be enough

insights.claim: A 2014 federal indictment accused Chinese military officers of hacking American firms including nuclear-reactor manufacturer Westinghouse as early as 2006, yet the Defense Department's threat-sharing program with cleared contractors was not formalized until 2012 — a delay the U.S. must not repeat as AI-stack companies become high-value foreign intelligence targets.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Historical base rate for U.S. counterintelligence response is roughly six years — assume AI labs stay under-protected for years, which is a real operational risk to frontier-lab IP value.
insights.locator: The United States must also urgently learn the lessons

insights.claim: Programs through which AI labs share their most cyber-capable models with select defenders should prioritize admitting the industrial control-system vendors whose products run U.S. water and energy infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: Watch vetted-access rosters expanding from tech and finance into ICS vendors — a signal of where hardening capex lands next.
insights.locator: The U.S. government, as well as infrastructure owners and operators, will have to motivate vendors

insights.claim: The author argues the president can order most of the proposed measures directly and work with Congress to fast-track a once-in-a-generation appropriation for critical-infrastructure security and resilience, meaning the constraint is political will rather than authority.
insights.speaker: Michael Sulmeyer
insights.so_what: If a large cyber-resilience appropriation materializes on this nine-to-12-month clock, OT-security and grid-hardening suppliers are the direct beneficiaries.
insights.locator: Projects to disrupt distillation and illegal access
